topic: Jumping and landing: training your knees for sport

slides.headline: How do your knees handle landing?
slides.sub: Jumping and landing are trainable skills. Here's where to start.

slides.title: Landing is where load peaks
slides.body: In netball, basketball, volleyball and touch, landings and sudden stops put big forces through the knee. Good control spreads that load across your hips, knees and ankles.

slides.title: Land soft and quiet
slides.body: Land on the balls of your feet and let your ankles, knees and hips bend together. Aim for a quiet landing, with knees tracking in line with your toes.

slides.title: Start with two feet
slides.body: Practise small jumps onto and off a low step, sticking each landing for two seconds. Once that feels controlled, add height, then single-leg hops, then direction changes.

slides.title: Strength underpins it all
slides.body: Squats, lunges, step-downs and calf raises build the capacity to absorb landings. Research suggests warm-up programs with strength and landing drills can reduce knee injuries in sport.

slides.title: When to get it checked
slides.body: A pop with swelling, your knee giving way, locking, or pain below or around the kneecap that builds with jumping is worth an assessment before you keep playing.

slides.headline: Train your landings

caption:
How do your knees handle landing? It's a skill you can train.

Jumping and landing put some of the biggest loads through your knees in sport, especially in netball, basketball, volleyball and touch. Good control spreads that load across your hips, knees and ankles.

Start by landing soft and quiet with knees in line with toes. Practise small two-foot jumps and stick each landing, then progress to single-leg hops and direction changes. Squats, lunges and step-downs build the strength behind it. A pop, swelling or knee giving way needs an assessment.

story.headline: Try this landing drill
story.body: Jump off a low step, land soft and quiet, knees over toes. Hold for two seconds. Ten reps.
